rows.why: Check the news first — we expect 3.2 but the line is 2.0. A gap this big usually means the sportsbook knows something (a role change, an injury). We expect about 3.2 passing TDs vs the 2.0 line. We give the over 60% (needs 57% per pick on PrizePicks); recent games and the matchup both point higher
rows.why_long: PrizePicks higher 2.0 needs 57% per pick for your entry; fair view 59% (fanduel 1.5, moved to this line). Averaging 3.2 over the last 8 games, higher than 2.0 in 76% of them (raw 77%, shrunk 60%). Projects 3.2 (raw 74%, shrunk 60%).
why_points: The pick: Pass TD higher 2.0 on PrizePicks. Each pick has to win 57% of the time for a typical entry to make money; the sportsbooks' fair view (fanduel 1.5, moved to this line) is 59%.
Game log, most recent first: 3, 5, 4, 4, 1, 3, 2, 1. Weighted average 3.2; went higher than 2.0 in 5 of 8 games (76% recency-weighted).
Trending up: last 3 games average 4.0 vs 2.2 in the games before.
How much he swings: game to game he typically moves about ±1.3, so the line is 0.9 of those swings below his average (standard deviations) — a meaningful gap.
Projection: we expect 3.2 passing TDs on average — 1.2 above the line.

Keeping it honest: on their own, recent games (form) say 77% and the matchup 74%. The sportsbooks are usually close to right, and these methods have only partly beaten them (weights measured on NFL week 2), so we pull them most of the way toward the market: form 60%, matchup 60%.
Bottom line: we give it 60% to win and it needs 57%. The edge is the difference: +3.2 points; that works out to about +6¢ per $1 bet over the long run.
Risks: low line - one play can decide it.
rows.glance_head: The over looks good: we expect about 3.2 on average vs the 2 line, and his recent games and the matchup agree.
